channel.title: The Grant Desk - Media Arts, Film & Sound, US, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Media Arts, Film & Sound, US, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Grant: Sundance Episodic Lab 2027: Alfred P. Sloan Grant Track (science and technology series) (closes 3 Dec)
item.description:
Sundance Institute with the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation
Deadline: 3 Dec 2026
Award: USD 17,000 grant plus creative support through the Episodic Lab. Submission fee waived with code EpSloanGrantX121426 on FilmFreeway.

An extended Sloan-only round of the Sundance Episodic Lab for original half-hour or one-hour series whose subject is science, technology or mathematics, or a scientist, engineer or mathematician. Open to a writer or a two-person writing team.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: Artists & Mothers Grant 2027: USD 25,000 for a year of childcare (New York City artist-mothers) (closes 4 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Artists & Mothers
Deadline: 4 Jan 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 25,000 to subsidise a year of childcare with the provider of the artist's choice. No application fee stated.

Artists & Mothers gives working artists who identify as mothers USD 25,000 to pay for a year of childcare with a provider of their choice, so they can keep making work at an inflection point in their careers.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: GLEAM 2027: Request for Light-Based Artwork Proposals (Olbrich Botanical Gardens; honorariums USD 5,000 to 30,000) (closes 6 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Olbrich Botanical Gardens (City of Madison Parks Division and Olbrich Botanical Society)
Deadline: 6 Jan 2027, 23:59 CST
Award: All-inclusive honorarium of USD 5,000 to 30,000 per artwork, covering artist fee, materials, fabrication, travel, lodging, install and maintenance. Usually only one USD 30,000 project is selected; proposals under USD 25,000 get the most consideration. Free host lodging and loan projectors and speakers are available. No application fee stated.

GLEAM is an annual night-time light art exhibition across a 16-acre botanical garden and a 10,000 sq ft tropical conservatory.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: NYSCA/Wave Farm Media Arts Assistance Fund (MAAF) for Artists 2027 (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Wave Farm (NYSCA regrant)
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: Up to USD 7,500. No application fee.

A NYSCA regrant run by Wave Farm supporting New York State artists to complete or present new sound and moving-image works, including work with emergent technologies.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Grant: Awesome Foundation Local Chapters: USD 1,000 Monthly Micro-grants (US, UK, Canada, Australia, NL, Asia) (rolling)
item.description:
Awesome Foundation (local chapters)
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Usually USD 1,000 (or local equivalent) per grant, no strings attached, typically one grant per chapter per month. No application fee.

The Awesome Foundation is a network of volunteer giving circles: in each chapter about ten trustees pool their own money to give a USD 1,000 no-strings micro-grant, usually monthly, to a project that adds "awesome" to their area: art, public interventions, community tech, events, science and civic...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Mabou Mines SUITE/space Residency 2027-2029 (NYC early-career interdisciplinary performance, two USD 4,000 stipends) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Mabou Mines
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Two USD 4,000 stipends (dependent on funding), plus 100 hours of rehearsal space and technical support. No application fee.

SUITE/space is Mabou Mines' two-year performance residency for early-career interdisciplinary artists in New York whose practices come from lived experiences at the margins. WHO: NYC-based early-career interdisciplinary performance artists.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: WVU Libraries Artist in Residence 2027: Common Threads, Industry, Labor and Community (USD 1,000 honorarium) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
West Virginia University Libraries
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: USD 1,000 honorarium plus up to USD 1,000 materials and up to USD 3,000 travel and lodging. No application fee.

An archive-based residency in which the artist works with WVU Libraries' union records and oral histories on industry, labor and community. Digital media is eligible. ELIGIBILITY: US- and Canada-based artists aged 18 and over.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Kent Cultural Alliance SFW Residency, Spring 2027 "SERVICE": six-week live-in residency in Chestertown, Maryland (USD 7,500 stipend) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Kent Cultural Alliance
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: USD 7,500 stipend for the six-week session, travel reimbursed up to USD 1,000, studio and gallery expenses reimbursed up to USD 1,500, and on-site housing with a private en-suite bedroom. No application fee.

A community-engaged residency on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Three artists live and work for six weeks in the Raimond Cultural Center, a restored historic house, around the theme SERVICE, working with local partners For All Seasons, the Kent County Food Pantry and Sumner Hall.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Glen Foerd Artist in Residence 2027: year-long residency for a Philadelphia performance artist or collective (USD 3,000 stipend) (closes 6 Dec)
item.description:
Glen Foerd
Deadline: 6 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 3,000 stipend for materials, time and costs, paid in three instalments. USD 10 application fee, waived on request.

Glen Foerd, a riverside historic estate in Philadelphia, selects one Philadelphia-based performance artist or collective for its 2027 residency. Performance is read broadly: music, theatre, film and social practice all count.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Petrides Residency for a Greek Artist in NY (NYFA x ISCP): funded three-month Brooklyn studio residency (USD 9,000 stipend) (closes 8 Dec)
item.description:
New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA) with sculptor George Petrides and the International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP)
Deadline: 8 Dec 2026, 17:00 EST
Award: Fully funded three-month residency with a private studio, a USD 9,000 stipend, a USD 1,000 travel payment and up to USD 300 for professional development. Housing is not arranged by ISCP. No application fee stated.

NYFA, sculptor George Petrides and the International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP) offer one Greek artist a fully funded three-month studio residency in Brooklyn.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Craigardan Trillium Fellowship 2027 (residency for artists, activists and scholars of color, USD 4,600 + USD 500 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Craigardan
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: USD 4,600 fellowship toward a minimum two-week residency (covers the residency fee), plus a USD 500 honorarium. Travel, materials and personal expenses are not covered. USD 25 application fee (waivers available on request).

The Trillium Fellowship supports artists, activists and scholars of color working in any discipline who would benefit from the time and space to pursue their work or find creative retreat at Craigardan, a residency and farm in the Adirondacks.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: EFA SHIFT x Momus Residency 2027: six-month programme for New York artists who write and writers who make art (USD 2,000 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts (EFA Studios) with Momus
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: Artist honorarium of USD 2,000, within a six-month residency at EFA Studios with monthly critical seminars and mentoring. No application fee stated.

A new iteration of EFA's SHIFT Residency, run with the art criticism platform Momus and focused on where artistic practice meets critical writing.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: SPACES: Echo Artist Residency (Cleveland, paired residency with honorarium and production budget) (closes 10 Feb 2027)
item.description:
SPACES
Deadline: 10 Feb 2027
Award: Artist honorarium and production budget plus lodging in the gallery. SPACES does not publish figures; the Alliance of Artists Communities listing gives a USD 2,000 artist stipend plus USD 500 for travel and materials. No application fee.

Echo is a paired residency at SPACES in Cleveland: each season it selects one Northeast Ohio artist (Cuyahoga and contiguous counties) and one artist from outside the region as a peer cohort, preferring complementary or intersecting themes, though collaboration is not required.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Residency: Kala Art Institute: Media Arts Fellowship 2027-28 (Berkeley; USD 3,000 stipend) (closes 1 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Kala Art Institute
Deadline: 1 Mar 2027
Award: USD 3,000 stipend plus facility access.

Kala's long-running Media Arts Fellowship supports four artists working in film and video, sound, animation, performance cinema and media installation. ELIGIBILITY: local, national and international artists not enrolled in a degree programme.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: Florence Levy Kay Postdoctoral Fellowship in Computer Music and Engineering (Brandeis University) 2027-2029 (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Brandeis University (Department of Music and Engineering)
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 64,000 for the nine-month year (lecturer rank), plus USD 4,000 a year for research and travel and negotiable first-year relocation. No application fee.

A two-year postdoctoral fellowship in computer music and engineering: human/machine music-making, signal processing, and instrument and interface design, hosted by Brandeis Music and Engineering.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fellowship: Folger Institute Artistic Research Fellowships 2027-28 (USD 4,000 to 5,000 per month) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Folger Shakespeare Library (Folger Institute)
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 4,000 per virtual month or USD 5,000 per onsite month.

Artistic research fellowships for artists whose work needs primary research on the early modern world (about 1400 to 1800) and its legacies, using the Folger's collections. ELIGIBILITY: any artist; no degree required and no citizenship rule stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Prize: Tag! Queer Shorts Festival 2027: Call for Submissions (Portland) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Tag! Queer Shorts Festival
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Award categories with cash prizes (amounts not stated): Hispanic/Latine Creativity, Power of Community, Best Erotic Short and Radical Futures Student Film, plus a Festival Director's Award. Modest submission fees on FilmFreeway; fee waivers for historically excluded communities and filmmakers from countries that criminalize queer identities, and discount codes for Pacific Northwest filmmakers.

Tag! invites LGBTQIA+ filmmakers to submit finished shorts of 15 minutes or under, including credits, in any genre (theme for 2027: "You're It!"). About 40 to 45 shorts are selected. English captions are required; films made with generative AI are not programmed; no works in progress.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Prize: AT&T Untold Stories 2027 (Tribeca Festival): USD 1.2 million film production prize (closes 18 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Tribeca Festival and AT&T
Deadline: 18 Jan 2027
Award: One winner receives USD 1,200,000 to produce the film; the four other finalists receive USD 15,000 grants each. No entry fee.

AT&T Untold Stories, now in its 10th year, is a production prize run by the Tribeca Festival and AT&T that funds a feature film from an underrepresented filmmaker. Industry judges select five projects; their filmmakers pitch to a jury of media professionals at the 2027 Tribeca Festival in June.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: Full Frame Documentary Film Festival 2027: Call for Entries (closes 15 Nov)
item.description:
Full Frame Documentary Film Festival
Deadline: 15 Nov 2026, 23:00 EST
Award: EXCEPTION: NOT FUNDED (festival call). Late-deadline fees USD 90 (features) or USD 70 (shorts); students USD 50 / 30. No fee waivers this year.

Full Frame takes documentaries completed after 1 January 2026, up to 180 minutes, for its 2027 festival. Late deadline 15 November 2026, 11 pm ET.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: Wide Open Experimental Film Festival 2027: Submissions (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Wide Open Experimental Film Festival (Oklahoma City University)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: EXCEPTION: NOT FUNDED (festival call). Late fee USD 25 via FilmFreeway; no screening or travel fees paid.

An experimental film festival taking works under 25 minutes from anywhere, with no premiere requirement. Late deadline 30 November 2026 via FilmFreeway.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: True/False Film Fest 2027: Features and Shorts Submissions (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
True/False Film Fest
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 20:00 CST
Award: Selected feature filmmakers receive an appearance stipend (amount not stated) plus travel and lodging; attending shorts directors get a stipend and pass. Final-deadline fees USD 95 (features) or USD 60 (shorts); students USD 75 / 45; fee-waiver requests by 20 November.

True/False, a nonfiction festival known for paying its filmmakers, takes 2026-27 features and shorts and welcomes non-traditional nonfiction such as series, audio and live performance. Final deadline 1 December 2026, 8 pm CT.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: Tribeca Festival 2027: Features, Shorts and Digital Creators Submissions (closes 3 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Tribeca Festival
Deadline: 3 Feb 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: EXCEPTION: NOT FUNDED (festival call). Fees: features USD 90 / 115, shorts USD 70 / 80, digital creators USD 40 / 60 (official / extended).

Tribeca takes feature, short and digital-creator submissions for 2027. Features: official 18 November 2026, extended 16 December 2026. Shorts and Digital Creators: official 2 December 2026, extended 3 February 2027. All at 11:59 pm ET. VR and AR work goes through Tribeca Games.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: Frameline51: San Francisco International LGBTQ+ Film Festival 2027 Submissions (closes 1 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Frameline
Deadline: 1 Mar 2027
Award: EXCEPTION: NOT FUNDED (festival call). Tiered submission fees on FilmFreeway.

Frameline, the largest and longest-running LGBTQ+ film festival, takes work of any length or genre about LGBTQ+ people.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: Social and Economic Justice Film Festival 2027: Call for Entries (closes 1 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Alliance for Social and Economic Justice
Deadline: 1 Mar 2027
Award: EXCEPTION: NOT FUNDED (festival call). No submission fee listed; no screening fees paid.

A small San Francisco festival taking shorts, mid-length and feature documentaries or fiction on poverty, worker justice, LGBTQ rights and related social-justice themes, with a Youth category for directors under 25. English subtitles required; premieres preferred.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Open call: Brooklyn Film Festival 2027: Experimental and Short Film Submissions (closes 13 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Brooklyn Film Festival
Deadline: 13 Mar 2027
Award: About USD 50,000 in awards across cash, products and services. Submission fees on FilmFreeway.

Brooklyn Film Festival takes shorts and experimental films for 2027; a film must be at least a New York premiere to compete. Deadlines: early 30 November 2026, regular 5 January, advanced 31 January, late 25 February, extended 13 March 2027.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: COLA-IMAP 2027-29: Independent Master Artist Projects, USD 10,000 (Los Angeles) (closes 13 Nov)
item.description:
City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs
Deadline: 13 Nov 2026
Award: USD 10,000 per artist (budget dependent). No application fee stated.

The City of Los Angeles Independent Master Artist Project (COLA-IMAP) grant supports established LA artists to create new work, presented publicly by the city.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest: Artist in Residence 2027 (Kentucky, USD 2,500 stipend) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest (Arts in Nature programme)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: USD 2,500 stipend, plus a furnished one-bedroom cabin (kitchen, bath, Wi-Fi), a studio near a 32-acre lake, staff support, and free or discounted classes and events. No application fee stated.

Annual residency in which artists live at Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest and create site-specific work inspired by total immersion in the natural environment. WHO: visual and mixed-media artists, including those working with sound and with performance that incorporates visual elements.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Sundance Institute: 2027 Graton Fellowship (USD 25,000 for California Native artists) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Sundance Institute, Indigenous Program
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 16:30 MST
Award: USD 25,000 cash grant to each of 2 fellows, plus a yearlong support programme. No application fee.

The Graton Fellowship, run by the Sundance Institute Indigenous Program, supports two Native storytellers from California tribes with an unrestricted cash grant and a year of creative and professional support from Sundance, including mentorship and access to Institute programmes.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston: Core Residency Program 2027-29 (USD 100,000 over 23 months, artists and critical writers) (closes 8 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Core Residency Program, Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (MFAH)
Deadline: 8 Jan 2027
Award: USD 100,000 (USD 50,000 per year) plus a health and wellness stipend, private studio, and free or discounted Glassell School classes. Application fee USD 12.

Two-year residency for exceptional, highly motivated emerging artists and critical writers committed to developing a sustainable practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: School for Advanced Research: Native Artist Fellowships 2027 (USD 15,000 plus Santa Fe residency) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
School for Advanced Research, Indian Arts Research Center
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027
Award: USD 15,000 stipend plus housing, studio space, a supplies allowance and travel. No application fee stated.

The Indian Arts Research Center at the School for Advanced Research offers three residential fellowships for Native American artists: the Eric and Barbara Dobkin Fellowship for Native women artists working in any media (including digital art and film/video), the Ronald and Susan Dubin Fellowship...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Netherland-America Foundation: Cultural Grant Program (1 February 2027 Cut-Off) (closes 1 Feb 2027)
item.description:
The Netherland-America Foundation (NAF)
Deadline: 1 Feb 2027
Award: Typically up to USD 5,000 per project, depending on scope and impact; higher amounts possible depending on available budget. No application fee.

The Netherland-America Foundation funds professional artistic and cultural projects that show a clear exchange between Dutch and American artists, institutions or audiences, such as exhibitions, performances and other cultural initiatives that promote dialogue and collaboration.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Vision Maker Media: Creative Shorts Fellowship (up to USD 25,000 for emerging Native filmmakers, rolling)
item.description:
Vision Maker Media
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Up to USD 25,000 production funding, plus USD 5,000 paid separately to the mentor. No application fee shown.

Vision Maker Media's Creative Shorts Fellowship funds emerging Native filmmakers to make a short film of 40 minutes or less (documentary, drama, experimental or animation), with guidelines inviting work that pushes the limits of art and technology.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: MIT Museum: BRAIN Programmatic Open Call (public programs)
item.description: MIT Museum · deadline 01 Nov 2026 · Up to USD 1,000 total per selected program, covering all costs including speaker and performer fees, travel, materials and equipment rental; proposals using external funding or smaller budgets welcome. The Museum sets ticket prices and keeps ticket revenue. No application fee.

item.description: The Netherland-America Foundation (NAF) · deadline 01 Nov 2026 · Typically up to USD 5,000 per project, depending on scope and impact; higher amounts possible depending on available budget. No application fee.

item.description: Fractured Atlas (Inciter Art) · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · USD 750 stipend per selected writer, paid by ACH deposit or check once the first draft is finished (a W-9 form is required). No submission fee.

item.title: Oregon Media Arts Fellowship 2026 (two USD 5,000 awards for Oregon media artists)
item.description: Portland Art Museum (PAM CUT) and Oregon Arts Commission · deadline 15 Nov 2026 · Two fellowships of USD 5,000 each, no matching funds required; paid within two months of notification. No application fee.

item.description: City of Palo Alto Public Art Program · deadline 16 Nov 2026 · Up to USD 9,000 per installation, for up to five installations. No application fee.

item.description: City of Palo Alto Public Art Program · deadline 16 Nov 2026 · USD 20,000 commission budget. No application fee.

item.description: Asian Cultural Council · deadline 10 Nov 2026 · Up to USD 35,000 for self-directed exploration and cultural exchange of 1 to 6 months. Single or joint applications (up to 3 participants). No application fee.

item.title: Asian Cultural Council New York Fellowship 2027 (USD 38,000)
item.description: Asian Cultural Council · deadline 10 Nov 2026 · USD 38,000 for the six-month fellowship, covering the immersive cultural exchange in New York City. No application fee.

item.title: LMCC Manhattan Arts Grants: Creative Engagement 2027
item.description: Lower Manhattan Cultural Council (LMCC) · deadline 12 Nov 2026 · USD 1,000 to 20,000 per grant for public arts events in Manhattan between January and December 2027. No application fee.

item.description: Adirondack Experience, The Museum on Blue Mountain Lake (ADKX) · deadline 11 Dec 2026 · USD 5,000 stipend per one-month residency, plus USD 500 travel allowance, USD 250 Art Lab materials allowance, and free on-site housing with utilities, wi-fi and laundry included.
